name: Business Case Builder
summary: Builds a business case for an investment: options including doing nothing, costs and benefits as stated, risks and a recommendation.
description: Structures a decision to spend money or effort (a hire, a tool, a project) into a business case: the problem, at least three options including doing nothing, the costs and benefits of each as you stated them, risks, the assumptions that matter most, and a recommendation that must name one of the options. A reviewer checks that the recommendation follows from the analysis. Who it's for: founders, managers and finance partners asking for budget or approval. Limitations: it does not compute NPV, ROI or payback; figures appear only as you supply them. Benefits you did not quantify stay qualitative.
problems: I need to justify a budget request
I need approval to hire or buy a tool
We decide on investments without comparing options

inputs.label: What you want to do
inputs.example: Hire a second support agent ($55k/yr) because response times doubled since January.

inputs.label: Costs and benefits you know
inputs.example: Median first response 9h (Jan: 4h). 3 churned accounts cited support in exit surveys.

outputs.label: Business case
outputs.description: Problem, options, costs and benefits, risks, assumptions and recommendation.

execution.system: You write decision-ready business cases. Always include doing nothing as an option. Present costs and benefits only as supplied or clearly labelled estimates to verify. The recommendation must follow from the comparison.

decision_needed.description: What the approver is asked to decide, by when.
decision_needed.title: Decision needed

steps.name: Build case
steps.prompt: Write the business case with 3-5 options (OPT1, ...), one of which is doing nothing. Use only the figures supplied; label anything else as an estimate to verify. Recommend one option by id, with the conditions under which you would change the recommendation.

steps.name: Check case
steps.responsibility: The recommendation names a listed option; options are distinct.

steps.name: Review reasoning
steps.responsibility: Grade whether the recommendation follows from the comparison.

criteria.description: The recommendation names one of the listed options.
The recommendation follows from the costs, benefits and risks presented.

review.rubric: Does the recommended option follow from the comparison, with trade-offs acknowledged, and no benefit or cost appearing only in the recommendation? 5 = clearly follows; 1 = contradicts or ignores the analysis.
